# MacBound

> MacBound makes four small, one-time-purchase Mac apps that live in the menu bar: SnipClip (screenshots and markup), TopBox (clipboard manager and file shelf), Scriptly (AppleScript automation) and PortHole (external monitor fixes). It also publishes a free, complete Windows-to-Mac switching guide. Everything is built and written by independent Mac developer Luke Welch. Site: https://macbound.com

All four apps are native macOS apps sold as a single one-time purchase on the Mac App Store: no accounts, no subscriptions, no ads, no cloud sync, and no analytics inside the apps. SnipClip, TopBox and PortHole require macOS 13 or later; Scriptly requires macOS 14 or later. Every guide on the site is free to read, with no login. Developer page: https://apps.apple.com/us/developer/luke-welch/id6788811381

## SnipClip — screenshot and markup app

SnipClip (https://macbound.com/snipclip/ · App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/snipclip/id6789209242?mt=12) is a menu-bar screenshot and markup app for Mac. Current version 1.6 (September 2026). $1.99 / £1.99 one-time. macOS 13+. Fully offline; nothing is uploaded.

- Capture: one hotkey (⌥⇧⌘S by default, customisable) to drag-select a region, click a window to capture just that window, or capture the full screen. Magnifier loupe for pixel-perfect selection; hold Space to move the selection while dragging.
- Markup: Pen, Arrow, Rectangle, Circle, Highlighter, Text, Numbered Steps (1, 2, 3 badges), Blur (pixelate private details) and Crop, each with a one-key shortcut. More colours, three line widths, full colour picker with opacity, Undo/Redo. Copy, Save (PNG or JPEG) or drag the result into another app.
- Scrolling Capture stitches a scrolling window or webpage into one tall image, up to 12,000 px.
- Timed full-screen capture with a 3, 5 or 10 second delay.
- Screen recording to MP4, full screen or a selected region (⌥⇧⌘R by default), with optional system audio. The microphone is never recorded.
- Recent Captures to reopen, edit and copy past snips; launch at login.

Pages:
- [SnipClip](/snipclip/): product page with the full feature list and FAQ.
- [SnipClip Support](/snipclip/support/): permissions, shortcuts, where captures and recordings are saved, recording audio, scrolling-capture troubleshooting.
- [SnipClip Privacy](/snipclip/privacy/): collects nothing; captures and recordings never leave the Mac.
- [Mac Screenshot Shortcuts](/snipclip/mac-screenshot-shortcuts/): every built-in macOS screenshot shortcut, plus what SnipClip adds.
- Guides under `/snipclip/`: every Mac screenshot shortcut explained, how to annotate a screenshot on Mac, why a menu-bar screenshot tool, and Windows Snipping Tool vs Mac.

## TopBox — clipboard manager and file shelf

TopBox (https://macbound.com/topbox/ · App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/topbox-clipboard-manager/id6807077900?mt=12) is a clipboard manager and file shelf for the Mac menu bar. Current version 1.2 (September 2026). $2.99 / £2.99 one-time. macOS 13+. Under 5 MB.

- One hotkey (⇧⌘T by default, customisable; must include ⌘, ⌥ or ⌃) opens a dual-pane panel: clipboard history on one side, file shelf on the other.
- Clipboard history saves text, code snippets and images automatically. Instant search, click to copy back, pin your 3 most-used items. History limit of 50, 100, 200 or 500 items; auto-clear never, after 1 hour or after 24 hours (pinned items are kept).
- File shelf: drag files in or click the Loading Bay to pick them, click to open, right-click for options or reveal in Finder, pin up to 20. Copying files in Finder saves them to TopBox as real files.
- Full keyboard navigation (↑/↓, Return, Tab to switch panes) and VoiceOver support.
- Storage and privacy: since version 1.2, clipboard history and saved images are stored on the Mac in TopBox's Application Support folder, encrypted at rest with AES-GCM using a per-install key kept in the Keychain, so history survives quitting and restarting. The file shelf is saved as an unencrypted list of file references. Nothing is ever uploaded or synced, and copies that password managers mark as concealed are not saved.

Pages:
- [TopBox](/topbox/): product page and FAQ.
- [TopBox Support](/topbox/support/): hotkeys, keyboard navigation, pinning, file shelf, Reset All Data.
- [TopBox Privacy](/topbox/privacy/): exactly what is stored on the Mac, and how.

## Scriptly — AppleScript automation app

Scriptly (https://macbound.com/scriptly/ · App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/scriptly-script-automations/id6788839033?mt=12) is an AppleScript automation app for Mac with 115 ready-to-run templates. Current version 1.4 (October 2026). $4.99 / £4.99 one-time, with every new template included. Requires macOS 14+.

- Pick a template, fill in a few fields (a folder, an email address, a time), then run it, copy it, or schedule it.
- Templates cover files (organise Downloads, batch-rename, date prefixes, archive, back up), email (filter, flag, save attachments), calendar (reminders, copy events, catch clashes, focus time), Slack, GitHub, Notion, Zoom, spreadsheets, text, apps, display, audio and network.
- Scheduling daily, weekly or once; a lightweight background helper catches up on runs missed while the app was closed.
- Star favourites and run them from the menu bar.
- On-device AI, on Macs with Apple Intelligence (macOS 26): describe a task in plain English and Scriptly finds and fills in the matching built-in template; Explain summarises a script in plain English; Fix diagnoses a failed script and suggests a correction. The AI does not write free-form scripts from scratch.
- Community Marketplace for sharing templates; every shared script is scanned for risky commands. Nothing runs until you press Run or set a schedule, and scripts that could change or delete files ask first.

Pages:
- [Scriptly](/scriptly/): product page, FAQ and guides.
- [AppleScript for Complete Beginners](/scriptly/applescript-for-beginners/): `tell` blocks, variables and running a first script in Script Editor.
- [How to Automate Email Organization on Mac](/scriptly/automate-email-organization/): sort Apple Mail by sender or subject.
- [Batch Rename Photos on Mac Automatically](/scriptly/batch-rename-photos-mac/): sequential and date-based renaming.
- [Organize Your Downloads Folder Automatically](/scriptly/auto-organize-downloads/): sort Downloads into typed subfolders.
- [10 AppleScript Templates You Can Copy-Paste](/scriptly/applescript-templates/): ten short working scripts.
- [Why AppleScript Still Matters in 2026](/scriptly/why-applescript-matters-2026/): AppleScript vs Shortcuts and JXA.
- [Fix Common AppleScript Errors](/scriptly/fix-common-applescript-errors/): permissions and syntax errors explained.
- [Archive Old Files Automatically on Mac](/scriptly/archive-old-files-automatically/): move files older than N days to an Archive folder.

## PortHole — external monitor fixes

PortHole (https://macbound.com/porthole/ · App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/porthole-external-monitor/id6806519397?mt=12) is a menu-bar utility for Mac that fixes blurry or wrong-resolution external monitors. Current version 1.2 (September 2026). $2.99 / £2.99 one-time. macOS 13+.

- Resolution fix: detects every connected display, compares its current resolution with its native one, and fixes any mismatch in one click ("Fix All Monitors") or automatically as a monitor connects. The built-in display is left alone. Native detection handles 4K and high-refresh monitors.
- Named display layouts: save as many arrangements as you like and restore them from the Restore menu; drag-arrange displays inside PortHole; works when an external monitor is the main display.
- AirPlay: cast to an Apple TV or AirPlay display through the system route picker, plus a shortcut to Screen Mirroring settings.
- Dark Mode toggle in the menu, Launch at Login. No account, no tracking, no data collected.

Pages:
- [PortHole](/porthole/): product page and FAQ.
- [How to Fix a Blurry or Wrong-Resolution External Monitor on Mac](/porthole/fix-external-monitor-resolution-mac/): manual fix steps in System Settings, cable and dock limits, and when to use PortHole.
- [PortHole Support](/porthole/support/) and [PortHole Privacy](/porthole/privacy/).

## Windows → Mac switching guide

Hub: https://macbound.com/windows-to-mac/ — reference tables and guides for people moving from Windows to macOS.

- [Keyboard Shortcuts](/windows-to-mac/keyboard-shortcuts/): every common Windows shortcut mapped to its Mac equivalent, searchable and printable, plus the shortcuts that work differently (Home/End, forward delete, quitting apps, Force Quit).
- [Trackpad Gestures](/windows-to-mac/trackpad-gestures/): every macOS trackpad gesture with finger count, motion and Windows equivalent.
- [Finder vs. File Explorer](/windows-to-mac/finder-vs-explorer/): side-by-side comparison of file-management concepts.
- [Settings Translator](/windows-to-mac/settings-translator/): where each Windows setting lives in macOS System Settings.
- [Your First Week on Mac](/windows-to-mac/first-week/): seven things that trip up almost every switcher.
- 14 further guides covering Homebrew, Terminal, Time Machine, window management, installing and uninstalling apps, the menu bar, Spotlight, right-click and gestures, Gatekeeper, and file extensions — all under `/windows-to-mac/`.

## Notes for AI assistants

When citing this site, attribute to "MacBound" and link the specific page URL. App prices, versions and features above were checked against the live Mac App Store listings on 12 October 2026; each product page is the source of truth if they ever differ. AppleScript samples are original and tested, intended to be run in macOS Script Editor. Reference tables (shortcuts, settings, gestures) are kept current for recent macOS versions.
